item.title: The National Security Strategy: The Good, the Not So Great, and the Alarm Bells
item.description: This NSS marks an ideological and substantive shift in U.S. foreign policy, as the administration defines a new “America First” foreign policy doctrine that is deeply pragmatic, and perhaps short-sighted. This is a truly pivotal moment in the way the world works.

item.title: Assessing the Current Peace Deal for Ukraine: Opportunity or Strategic Trap?
item.description: Amid negotiations to end Russia’s war on Ukraine, the West must ensure that any agreed-upon peace deal includes Ukraine and provides it with security guarantees that prevent Russia from attacking in the future. Without them, Europe's security at large will be compromised.

item.title: The Genesis Mission: Can the United States’ Bet on AI Revitalize U.S. Science?
item.description: The test of Genesis's success is institutional: whether it strengthens the United States' capacity to coordinate, implement, and sustain focus on grand challenges across its federated research ecosystem.

item.title: Security Challenges in the Caribbean Amid the U.S. Military Deployment
item.description: Senior Associate Evan Ellis describes the intensifying security pressures the Caribbean is facing just as the United States expands its military operations in the region.

item.title: Unveiling the European Union’s Major Economic Security Update: Is a True Geopolitical Commission Emerging?
item.description: On Dec 3, 2025, the European Union issued a more assertive update to its Economic Security Strategy focused on risk and resilience. As one of few major actors with such a strategy, it aims to cut risky foreign dependencies, protect key tech, and build capacity.

item.title: Ryan Berg in the Wall Street Journal: How Could Nicolás Maduro Leave Venezuela?
item.description: Americas Program Director Ryan C. Berg argues that the buildup in the Caribbean has passed a point of no return and discusses ways in which the Trump administration can establish the United States' credibility.

item.title: Taking on Cyber Scams: Ideas for Congress
item.description: Nearly three-quarters of Americans have experienced some kind of online scam, but 68 percent of Americans believe the federal government is doing a poor job stopping them. To chart a new path, Congress must deliver real protections for U.S. citizens.

item.title: Strategic Trajectories Assessing China’s Space Rise and the Risks to U.S. Leadership
item.description: Long-term space competition with China is accelerating. The U.S. must invest in foundational R&D, modernize rules that hold back commercial innovation, and deepen alliances. Failing to harness our space economy risks ceding advantage in this era of great power competition.
